nameStory: The green lynx spider gets its name from its brilliant green coloration and its hunting style - it pounces on prey with the agile, cat-like movements of a wild lynx. Like its feline namesake, this spider is a patient stalker that relies on quick reflexes and powerful leaps to catch its meals.
description: The green lynx spider is a vibrant, bright-green hunting spider that lives exclusively on plants. Unlike web-building spiders, this active predator stalks and pounces on its prey during daylight hours. It's primarily a southern species, making it an extremely rare and exciting find in New England, with only one confirmed observation in our region.

idTips.label: Color
idTips.description: Brilliant bright green body that perfectly matches fresh plant foliage - so vivid it almost looks artificial or painted

idTips.label: Behavior
idTips.description: Moves with quick, jerky motions across plant surfaces and pounces on prey like a tiny cat - no web building

idTips.label: Habitat
idTips.description: Always found on green vegetation, never on bark, rocks, or ground - seems to prefer flowers and leafy plants

idTips.label: Body Shape
idTips.description: Lean, athletic build with long, spiny legs that feel slightly rough to the touch if handled

idTips.label: Activity
idTips.description: Active during bright daylight hours when most spiders are hidden - easy to spot moving in full sun

habitat: In New England, this would be an extraordinary vagrant find, likely on flowering plants or shrubs in the warmest, most protected locations. Given its southern distribution, any New England sighting would probably be in coastal areas or urban heat islands where temperatures stay warmest.

seasonality.spring: Extremely unlikely to be present, as this southern species cannot survive New England winters.
seasonality.summer: The only season when a vagrant individual might possibly survive temporarily in New England's warmest microclimates.
seasonality.fall: Any summer vagrant would not survive the cooling temperatures of fall in our region.
seasonality.winter: Cannot survive New England winters - this species requires year-round warm temperatures.

funFact: Green lynx spiders are so perfectly camouflaged on plants that they can actually spit venom up to 8 inches to defend themselves - making them one of the few spiders that can launch a ranged attack!
confusionNotes: The brilliant green color makes this spider nearly unmistakable - no other New England spider is this vivid green. Green crab spiders are much paler and have a completely different body shape and leg arrangement.
contextualKnowledge: This spider's presence in New England would be so unusual that any sighting should be photographed and reported to local naturalists - it represents the extreme northern edge of climate change range expansion for southern species.
compareHints: As the only Peucetia species likely to reach New England, compare it instead to other lynx spiders in the Oxyopidae family. Other lynx spiders in our region are typically brown, gray, or pale colored and much less vibrant. The green lynx's electric green coloration and plant-specific habitat make it unique among all New England spiders.
